[Source · 2018]{.type-badge}

**Authors** — [Erik Brynjolfsson](/people/erik-brynjolfsson.qmd), Daniel Rock & Chad Syverson  ·  *NBER Working Paper 25148*

## Why it's here
The formal engine under David's history. GPTs demand large **intangible investment** the
national accounts don't capture, so productivity is *underestimated* while the intangibles
are built and *overestimated* when they're harvested — a J-curve. This is the model that
turns "the trough looks like failure" from a metaphor into a measurable claim.

::: {.pull-source}
"…this leads to an underestimation of productivity growth in the early years of a new GPT,
and… later, when the benefits of intangible investments are harvested, productivity growth
will be overestimated."

[— Brynjolfsson, Rock & Syverson, 2018]{.attribution}
:::
